title: Executive Power
tagline: Men who reached the top of Western institutions and stayed themselves. Proof the room can be entered without being swallowed by it.

entries.name: Barack Obama
entries.from: Honolulu, Hawaii (father from Nyang'oma Kogelo, Kenya)
entries.claim: Community organizer on Chicago's South Side who became the first Black president of the United States — and the first to write his own code into the White House website on day one.
entries.receipts: Obama's campaign built a custom community platform (MyBO) that registered over a million voters online. His White House relaunched WhiteHouse.gov on Drupal in 2009 and pushed the first open-source contributions from the Executive Branch to GitHub. Nobel Peace Prize, 2009. Two terms, 65.9 million popular votes in 2012.
entries.the_transfer: Community organizer to the presidency. That's the ceiling of what this repo's skills touch — organizing people, building tools, moving them online. Obama didn't code the site himself; he understood what code could DO for organizing. You're learning both sides: the organizing (pinned issues, welcome threads, DAP culture) and the tools (this whole repo).

entries.name: Kofi Annan
entries.self_note: FED-EDU covers all Black men worldwide — African leaders belong in the room.
entries.claim: Career diplomat who rose from budget officer to the first Black Secretary-General of the United Nations, then won the Nobel Peace Prize for rebuilding the UN's standing after its darkest decade.
entries.receipts: Secretary-General, 1997–2006 (two terms). Nobel Peace Prize, 2001 (shared with the UN). The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria — co-architect; it has since saved over 50 million lives. The Kofi Annan Foundation continues his mediation work.
entries.the_transfer: Annan ran the world's most impossible bureaucracy without ever raising his voice. His weapon: process. He would walk into a room of warring factions and negotiate one small agreement, then the next. That's exactly how big software gets built — one PR at a time, one review at a time, never trying to merge the whole war at once.

entries.name: Colin Powell
entries.self_note: Jamaican representation matters to the mission — our fathers' line runs through Kingston.
entries.claim: ROTC cadet from City College who rose to four-star general, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs, and the first Black Secretary of State.
entries.receipts: National Security Advisor at 41. Chairman of the Joint Chiefs during the Gulf War — the youngest man in the room and the one in charge. Secretary of State, 2001–2005. His 13 Rules of Leadership are taught in business schools and barracks alike.
entries.the_transfer: Powell's rules map straight onto engineering. Rule 8: 'Check small things.' That's unit tests. Rule 9: 'Share credit.' That's the DAP. Rule 2 and 3: get mad then get over it — that's code review without ego. Print his 13 rules next to your monitor; they were written for soldiers and they work for engineers.

entries.name: Thurgood Marshall
entries.claim: The attorney who argued Brown v. Board of Education before the Supreme Court, then became the Court's first Black justice.
entries.receipts: Brown v. Board, 1954 — the unanimous decision that struck down school segregation. As NAACP LDF counsel he won 29 of the 32 cases he argued before the Supreme Court. Nearly a quarter-century on the bench defending the rights the country kept trying to walk back.
entries.the_transfer: He prepared every case like the outcome was already decided and he just had to reveal it. He knew the record cold — the receipts were his weapon. Every PR you ship with tests, screenshots, and a clean diff is Thurgood Marshall discipline: build a record nobody can argue with.

entries.name: Arthur Ashe
entries.claim: The only Black man to win the US Open, Wimbledon, and the Australian Open — a decade after being barred from Richmond's white-only tennis courts as a kid.
entries.rebuttal_to_gatekeeping: Ashe's game was built on patience, math, and a flat first serve that read like logic. He proved the 'not athletic enough for the style' whisper wrong by out-thinking everyone on the tour.
entries.receipts: Three Grand Slam singles titles. Davis Cup captain — the first Black captain in the event's history. Off-court: he led the anti-apartheid protest that got South Africa expelled from the Davis Cup; after his AIDS diagnosis from a transfusion he became the face of calm public health education, founding the Arthur Ashe Foundation.
entries.the_transfer: Ashe was denied the courts in his own city, so he practiced on smaller fenced courts and read everything. Denied courts ≠ denied game. The brother denied a laptop is not denied the skill — this repo runs on a phone. Barriers tell you what to build around, and Ashe's whole career is the case study.

entries.name: Adam Clayton Powell Jr.
entries.claim: Congressman from Harlem who weaponized parliamentary procedure to force federal money into jobs, schools, and hospitals for Black America.
entries.receipts: Chairman of the Education and Labor Committee — legislation under his gavel included the minimum wage increase, Title I education funding, and the 1964 Civil Rights Act through his committee. He attached an anti-discrimination clause to federal contracts that forced northern cities to hire Black tradesmen or lose the money.
entries.the_transfer: Powell learned the rules better than the men who wrote them, then used the rules to force the change. That is EXACTLY what a senior engineer does with a codebase: knows the architecture cold, then changes the system from inside instead of raging at it. Learn the rules deep enough to bend them legally.
